name: Romam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Tạ Văn Thông & Tạ Quang Tùng. 2019. Cách gọi và cách viết tên ngôn ngữ các dân tộc ở Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu Dân tộc 8(1).
sources.note: Only lists the name 'Rơ Măm (Rơmăm)' (no. 52) and its Bahnaric affiliation.
Grep for Romam/Ramam/Rơ Măm/Lamam: no hits.
Zero descriptive references; cites only WRITENET 2002 (subclassification comment) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment).

sources.citation: OLAC. Resources in and about rmx (language-archives.org).
sources.note: One resource only: the Glottolog roma1331 record. No archived recordings or descriptions.

sources.citation: SEALang Mon-Khmer Languages Database, language list and MKLP lexical-sources list.
sources.note: No Romam/Ramam wordlist in the database; the source list has only 'Kacho'/Lamam: Crowley, James Dale, ms.' (Cambodian Kachok).

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2024. CLDF dataset derived from the Bahnaric data in Sidwell's 'Austroasiatic dataset for phylogenetic analysis' (2015), variety Ramam (roma1331). Lexibank / Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13162996.
sources.note: Segment inventory chart and wordlist derived from Sidwell 2015; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2015. Austroasiatic dataset for phylogenetic analysis: 2015 version. Mon-Khmer Studies 44: lxviii-ccclvii.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist only; 'Ramam rmx 86.5 Sidwell ms. Fieldnotes.' (p. lxxiv) is the source line. IPA forms (e.g. kətɔh, pətuk, həmɯl, təhãːj) show unstressed schwa presyllables but no stress marking or prose on stress.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii.
sources.note: p. xxxv: 'Romam is only briefly mentioned in the Ethnologue, but is not discussed in any known English language sources.' p. xxxvii, family-level only: 'Phonological words in Bahnaric may be mono- or disyllabic, with the latter generally treated as sesquisyllablic (iambic stress).' No Romam-specific data; lists Romam rmx as EGIDS 6a (p. lxii).

sources.citation: Võ Đức Tám. [c. 2013-2014, undated]. Âm tiết trong tiếng Rơ-măm [Syllable in Rơ-măm language]. 8 pp. MA-programme paper, Lớp Cao học ngôn ngữ K2012, Khoa Ngữ Văn, Trường Đại học Khoa học, Đại học Huế. Vietnamese with English summary.
sources.note: Nothing explicit: no occurrence of 'trọng âm' (stress) or 'nhấn'. Describes a sesquisyllabic word: monosyllable = major syllable (ÂTC); polysyllable = minor syllable/presyllable (ÂTP, CV(C) or nasal N) + major syllable, presyllable always first; major syllable is the 'nucleus' (hạt nhân), presyllable vowel is a neutral schwa that often deletes in connected speech (pp. 2-6). Classifies Rơ-măm as 'cận âm tiết tính' (sesquisyllabic) per Nguyễn Quang Hồng (p. 6). Author states no prior structural description of Rơ-măm exists (p. 1).

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project. Romam (ELP 5345): language page, resource pages and bibliography.
sources.note: No linguistic content; lists three resources (Lexibank Ramam wordlist; vi.wiktionary Rơ Măm category; 'Syllabic structure of the Rơ Măm language' = the Võ Đức Tám PDF). ELP bibliography cites only World Oral Literature Project and Glottolog.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng Rơ Măm' and Wikipedia (en) 'Kacoʼ language'.
sources.note: No phonology; references are Glottolog, Đặng Nghiêm Vạn et al. 2010, Magaspag 2012 (Kachok survey).
